papers.title: Sharp Holder regularity for autonomous Beltrami equations
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb C$ be a domain and let $\mathcal H:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ be Lipschitz with constant $0<k<1$. We prove that every weak $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ solution of the autonomous Beltrami equation $f_{\bar z}=\mathcal H(f_z)$ belongs to $C^{1,\gamma}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, where $\gamma=3/(2K+1)$ and $K=(1+k)/(1-k)$. The exponent is optimal, resolving the conjecture of Astala, Clop, Faraco, J\"a\"askel\"ainen and Koski.

papers.title: On the hyperplane conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the hyperplane conjecture, proposed by Hosono, Lian, and Yau in arXiv:alg-geom/9511001 and its generalization to orbifolds. Consequently, this establishes the expected equivalence between the \(A\) model (genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants with ambient insertions) of \(X\) and the \(B\) model (period integrals corresponding to vanishing cohomology) of \(X^{\vee}\) for Batyrev's mirror pair of Calabi--Yau hypersurfaces. As an application of our method, we also identify the residue of the Gauss--Manin connection and the cup product morphism on the \(A\)-side.

papers.title: Semi-classical Szeg\H{o} kernel asymptotics on CR manifolds of high codimension
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a CR manifold $X$ of high codimension and a CR line bundle $L$ over $X$. For each $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $L^k$ denote the $k$-th power of $L$. We establish that the spectral projection $\Pi_{k,\leq k\mu_k} := \mathbf{1}_{(-\infty, k\mu_k]}(\Box_{b,k})$ converges to the weighted Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions, where $\Box_{b,k}$ denotes the Kohn Laplacian with values in $L^k$. Moreover, when $\Box_{b,k}$ possesses a local spectral gap, we show that the Szeg\H{o} projection $\Pi_k$ converges to the weighted Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions. We also provide an explicit formula for the Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group. Furthermore, we consider a high codimension CR manifold $X$ equipped with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action. In this setting, we prove that the partial Szeg\H{o} projection $\Pi_{k,({\mathbb R}^m\curvearrowright,\leq k\delta)}$ converges to the weighted partial Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ topology. As an application of our results, we establish a Kodaira embedding theorem for high codimension CR manifolds with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action.

papers.title: Equidistribution, multipliers, and moving targets in polynomial families
papers.abstract: We study equidistribution of parameters for each of which a polynomial has a cycle with a prescribed moving multiplier in the full critically marked or unicritical polynomial families of a given degree $d>1$. For the full critically marked monic polynomial family $f=(f_\lambda)$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}^{d-1}$, of degree $d$, letting $p_{f,n}^*(\lambda,w)$ be the multiplier polynomial for cycles of formal exact period $n$ having multiplier $w$, we show that for any target sequence $w_n=d^na_n$ satisfying $n^{-1}\log|a_n|\to\ell\in[-\infty,+\infty)$, the averaged current of integration $\nu(n)^{-1}[p_{f,n}^*(\cdot,w_n)=0]$ along the zero divisor of $p_{f,n}^*(\cdot,w_n)$ tends to the $(1,1)$-current $\mathrm{d}\mathrm{d}^c\max\{L_d,\log d+\ell\}$ in the sense of currents on $\mathbb{C}^{d-1}$ as $n\to\infty$, where $L_d$ is the Lyapunov exponent function and $\nu(n)$ is the degree of the $n$th formal exact dynatomic polynomial associated to $f$. We also obtain the corresponding equidistribution theorem for the unicritical family $f_\lambda(z)=z^d+\lambda$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$, of degree $d$. The proof combines thermodynamic formalism, the Eremenko--Levin multiplier bound, and a comparison principle for plurisubharmonic functions, in a partly quantitative manner. A key ingredient is the vanishing of the bifurcation measure on the boundary of every component of the interior of the connectedness locus for the full critically marked family, which we show using Kiwi's study of critical portraits and rational laminations.

papers.title: Upper bounds on the number of images produced by point-mass lenses at different distances
papers.abstract: If a light source is sequentially lensed by $n$ intervening point-mass lenses at distinct distances, the number of isolated images for a generic source position cannot be greater than $2\cdot 3^{n-1}$. If lensing shear is present in each lens plane, the image counts could be as large as $4^n$, however. For a general multi-plane point-mass lens system, we also devise the recurrence for the BKK bound on the image counts, which is strictly less than Perry's bound due to the resultant degree for $n\ge 2$. None the less, this bound is still quadratic in the number of lenses on each plane, so is likely to overestimate the true sharp bound, which is expected to grow linearly with the number of lenses.

papers.title: Quadratic growth rigidity for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation
papers.abstract: For the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation on $\mathbb{C}^{n}$, we prove the Liouville theorem for solutions with quadratic growth.

papers.title: Levi Flat Structures via Structure Sheaves: Differential Complexes, Convexity, and Global Solvability
papers.abstract: This paper investigates Levi flat structures from the perspective of structure sheaves. We employ formal integrability to construct a class of differential complexes, thereby providing a resolution of the structure sheaf and a global realization of the Treves complex. Drawing inspiration from Morse theory and Grauert's convexity, we introduce notions of convexity and positivity that fully exploit Levi flatness, which yield global exactness of the differential complex and Sobolev regularity in the compact case. As applications, we establish the global solvability of the Treves complex for Levi flat structures, together with results on singular cohomology and the extension problem for canonical forms in the elliptic case.

papers.title: Envelope of Holomorphy of Matsuki Orbits in Complex Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We study the envelopes of holomorphy of Matsuki orbits $M_{\ell,m,r}$ arising as intersections of $G_0$- and $K$-orbits in complex Grassmannians. These orbits, equipped with natural CR-structures, form a class of compact homogeneous CR-submanifolds whose analytic continuation properties are of fundamental interest. Building on Rossi's theory of holomorphic extension, we establish that the envelope of holomorphy of each Matsuki orbit coincides biholomorphically with the containing $K$-orbit $O_{\ell,m}$. Our approach provides a geometric proof based on the holomorphic fiber bundle structure $\pi : M_{\ell,m,r} \to \mathrm{Gr}_{\ell}(E_+) \times \mathrm{Gr}_{m}(E_-)$, clarifying the role of compact isotropic fibers in constraining holomorphic extension. Explicit examples, including the orbit $M_{1,1,1} \subset \mathrm{Gr}_3(\mathbb{C}^8)$, illustrate the method and highlight connections with classical constructions in complex geometry and representation theory.

papers.title: Two-parameter Toeplitz-type operators between Fock spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce and study a two-parameter family of Toeplitz-type operators $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ on the Fock space $F^p(C)$ for $0<p\leq\infty$. For all $0<p, q \leq\infty$ we obtain sharp conditions for $\varphi$ such that $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi: F^p(C)\to F^q(C)$ is bounded or compact. In the Hilbert space case $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi: F^2(C)\to F^2(C)$, we also study the Berezin transform of $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ and membership of $T^{(s,t)}_\varphi$ in Schatten classes. Furthermore, we find a class of noncompact operators whose Berezin transforms nevertheless vanish at infinity.

papers.title: Asymptotics of Weighted Bergman Polynomials under Finite Regularity
papers.abstract: We study strong asymptotics of planar orthogonal polynomials with respect to fixed weighted area measures on Jordan domains. The aim is to understand how the regularity of the domain and the weight enter the large-degree asymptotic behavior of these polynomials. For domains with real-analytic boundaries, Suetin established leading-order asymptotics for H\"older continuous weights, while Hedenmalm--Wennman obtained a full asymptotic expansion for real-analytic weights. We interpolate between these results while allowing both the boundary and the weight to have finite smoothness. The resulting expansions have a length determined by the available regularity and hold in the exterior region and, under sufficient regularity conditions, in a shrinking neighborhood of the boundary.

papers.title: A least-squares lower bound for capacity
papers.abstract: We establish a least-squares lower bound for the logarithmic capacity of an arbitrary compact plane set, extending an inequality previously known for connected sets. The bound generalizes classical inequalities involving area and moment of inertia. It is sharp for disks, and asymptotically sharp for compact sets whose capacity coincides with that of their interior. We further show that asymptotic sharpness holds for general compact sets if we replace logarithmic capacity by minimal carrier capacity.

papers.title: Local Nevanlinna embedding for Hardy space of Dirichlet series below critical exponent
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate a problem posed by Saksman and Seip [ Contemp. Math., 2016] on whether functions in the Hardy space of Dirichlet series $\mathcal{H}^p$, \(0<p<2\), are locally in the Nevanlinna class of the critical half-plane \(\mathbb C_{1/2}\). We show that the local Nevanlinna embedding fails below critical exponent \(p=2\) by constructing $\mathcal{H}^p$-functions whose local logarithmic mass becomes unbounded as \(\real s\to 1/2^+\). This also clarifies the distinction between global Jessen-type logarithmic control and local boundary Nevanlinna behavior for Dirichlet series.

papers.title: Pseudoconvex Exhaustions of Hartogs Domains Associated with $L^2$-Optimal Pairs
papers.abstract: By constructing a smooth pseudoconvex exhaustion of the associated Hartogs domain, we give a new proof of the Deng-Ning-Wang's characterization of plurisubharmonic functions without the smoothness assumption.

papers.title: Non-abelian LVM manifolds}
papers.abstract: We extend the tangency construction of L\'opez de Medrano, Verjovsky and Meersseman from diagonal abelian actions to non-abelian Samelson groups. For these groups the tangency locus is a moment-map zero set: the commutator term in the leafwise Hessian vanishes there, and under an admissibility hypothesis, Kempf--Ness convexity gives a global transversal whose projectivization is a compact complex manifold. The construction includes compact rotation groups and groups with non-closed central rotations. In the latter setting we construct explicit families of complex dimension $2m-3$, $m\geq5$, which are $4$-connected and admit no symplectic form. Their meromorphic function fields are rational of transcendence degree $m-2$, although every holomorphic map to a projective space is constant. We compute their connected automorphism groups and show that they admit no maximal torus action. They are Hopf-surface bundles over compact complex quotients of stable Grassmannian loci; these bases give related examples already in complex dimension five. The families demonstrate that the non-abelian tangency construction reaches beyond compact complex manifolds with maximal torus actions.

papers.title: Integrable distortion I: Weil--Petersson circle homeomorphisms and the Schoen conjecture
papers.abstract: A circle homeomorphism $\beta:\mathbb{S}\to\mathbb{S}$ is Weil--Petersson if it has a quasiconformal disk extension whose Beltrami coefficient is square integrable for hyperbolic area. We minimise the hyperbolic anti-holomorphic energy \[ E_2(h)=\int_\mathbb{D}\eta(h)|h_{\bar w}|^2,dA, \quad\text{equivalently}\quad \int_\mathbb{D}\frac{|\mu_f|^2}{1-|\mu_f|^2},dA_\eta,\quad f=h^{-1}, \] over all monotone Sobolev maps with boundary values $\beta$. For Weil--Petersson data, the unique minimiser is a real analytic hyperbolic harmonic diffeomorphism, globally quasiconformal and asymptotically conformal, with an explicit dilatation bound in terms of any admissible barrier's energy. We prove that a circle homeomorphism is Weil--Petersson if and only if it admits a finite-distortion homeomorphic extension satisfying \[ \int_\mathbb{D}(\mathbb{K}_F-1),dA_\eta<\infty. \] For every $p>1$, the boundary values of a finite-distortion homeomorphism satisfying \[ \int_\mathbb{D}|\mu_F|^p(1-|\mu_F|^2)^{-p_*/2},dA_\eta<\infty \] lie in Guo's $p$-integrable Teichm"uller space $T^p$. A capacity estimate for boundary moduli for the quasisymmetric ratio yields a derivative-free characterisation of $T^p$, essentially Bishop's theorem when $p=2$. The minimum defines a M"obius-invariant boundary energy, quantitatively comparable to the weighted square norm of the minimiser's Hopf differential. For arbitrary quasisymmetric data, we prove Markovi'c's theorem (the Schoen conjecture) by approximation with our smooth quadratic minimisers. Mori's theorem and the mean-value property of a logarithm verify the averaged-distance hypothesis in Riestenberg--Smillie's interior comparison, giving explicit displacement, energy-density and dilatation bounds in terms of the quasisymmetry constant. The nonquadratic ($p\neq2$) theory is developed in Part~II.

papers.title: An intrinsic notion of visibility and classification of planar Denjoy-Wolff domains
papers.abstract: In this article, we introduce an intrinsic notion of visibility with respect to the Kobayashi distance that does not require any boundary. We establish localization results for the Kobayashi distance on Kobayashi hyperbolic domains in $\mathbb{C}^d$ that satisfy this intrinsic visibility property. As an application of these localization results, we compare the Busemann horospheres of a domain with those of a subdomain. Recently, Benini and Bracci characterized simply connected planar domains with the Denjoy-Wolff property in terms of Busemann horospheres. More precisely, they proved that a proper simply connected planar domain has the Denjoy-Wolff property if and only if the closure of every Busemann horosphere meets the boundary of the domain in exactly one point. We introduce Condition (M$\star$), a condition of attaching a proper disk to the domain at a boundary point. Using our localization results together with this comparison of Busemann horospheres, we extend the characterization of Benini and Bracci to domains satisfying Condition (M$\star$) at every boundary point, and to domains satisfying it outside a totally disconnected subset of the boundary. In particular, we obtain a characterization for finitely connected domains and for a large class of infinitely connected domains having the Denjoy-Wolff property. These characterizations yield a variety of domains with the Denjoy-Wolff property, which we illustrate through example.

papers.title: K\"ahler-Finsler rigidity of the Kobayashi metric and the K\"ahler base of weakly K\"ahler-Finsler metrics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a rigidity theorem: for every balanced, smooth, bounded pseudoconvex domain, its Kobayashi metric is a smooth, strongly pseudoconvex, K\"ahler-Finsler metric restricted on a neighborhood of the origin if and only if the domain is a Hermitian ellipsoid, biholomorphic to the unit ball. Thus for any balanced, smooth, bounded, strictly convex, and strongly pseudoconvex domain that is not biholomorphic to the unit ball, its Kobayashi metric is a non-K\"ahler-Finsler, weakly K\"ahler-Finsler metric. We also prove that the base manifold of every weak K\"ahler-Finsler metric is K\"ahler.

papers.title: On the group of automorphisms of the escaping sets of H\'{e}non maps
papers.abstract: In this article, we provide an explicit description of $\operatorname{Aut}_1(I_H^+)$, the group of automorphisms of the escaping set $I_H^+$ of a H\'enon map that induce the identity on its fundamental group. More precisely, for a H\'enon map $H(x,y)=(y,p(y)-\delta x),$ where $p$ is a polynomial of degree $d\geq 2$ and $\delta\neq 0$, we show that $\operatorname{Aut}_1(I_H^+)$ is completely determined by the degree and the coefficients of $p$. Thus, the automorphism group of the escaping set, subject to the prescribed topological constraint, can be explicitly characterized in terms of the underlying H\'enon map.

papers.title: A characterization of Griffiths semipositivity by top-degree optimal $\bar \partial$-estimates
papers.abstract: We prove that a singular Hermitian metric $h$ on a vector bundle agrees almost everywhere with a Griffiths semipositive metric if its dual metric $h^*$ is locally integrable and the $\bar \partial$-equation admits solutions with optimal $L^2$-estimates for $(n,n)$-forms, where $n$ is the dimension of the base manifold. In particular, under this integrability assumption, Nakano semipositivity in the sense of optimal estimates implies Griffiths semipositivity.

papers.title: A proof of the Baranov--Bessonov--Kapustin conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Baranov, Bessonov and Kapustin: for a non-constant inner function $\theta$, every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on the model space $K_\theta$ has a bounded symbol if and only if $\theta$ is one-component

papers.title: Invertible non-cyclic functions in the little Bloch space
papers.abstract: This paper presents a method for exhibiting functions $F$ in the little Bloch space $\B_0$ which are invertible, in the sense that $1/F$ also belongs to $\B_0$, and yet fail to be cyclic for the forward shift. The functions obtained in this way give rise to shift-invariant subspaces in $\B_0$ of index two, of a special type. The approach rests on a harmonic-measure criterion for non-cyclicity. This criterion gives a new manifestation of a principle of Borichev and Hedenmalm, and applies in a broad class of spaces of analytic functions.

papers.title: Invariance of logarithmic plurigenera and adjoint volumes in K\"ahler families
papers.abstract: We consider smooth proper families of compact complex manifolds over a disk whose total space is K\"ahler, together with a boundary divisor with relative simple normal crossings. We prove that, if the boundary is a rational divisor with coefficients in $[0,1)$, every logarithmic pluricanonical form on a fiber extends to a neighborhood of that fiber, and hence that the logarithmic plurigenera are constant. No positivity of the log canonical class is assumed. We prove further that, for real boundary coefficients in $[0,1]$, a log-adjoint class twisted by a smooth semipositive form has the same volume on every fiber, and that it is pseudoeffective either on every fiber or on none. When the log-adjoint class is nef on every fiber, we give a second proof of the extension theorem, which does not use the minimal model program.

papers.title: Functional Model for Isometric Pairs Satisfying an Automorphic Covariance Relation - I
papers.abstract: We derive a canonical functional model for a pair of isometric operators $(V_1, V_2)$ acting on a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ that satisfy the automorphic covariance relation $V_1 V_2 = V_2 \varphi(V_1)$, where $\varphi$ is an automorphism of the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$. This extends the classical Bercovici--Douglas--Foias functional model for commuting isometric pairs to a dynamically twisted setting. When both $V_1$ and $V_2$ are pure isometries (shifts), the model simplifies to $(M_z, M_{\Theta} W_\varphi^*)$ acting on $H^2(\mathcal{F})$, where $W_\varphi$ is a unitary weighted composition operator on the Hardy space $H^2$ and $\Theta \in H^\infty(\mathbb{D}, \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{F}))$ is an operator-valued inner function such that $M_{\Theta}$ is a shift. As an application, we establish a complete unitary classification theorem for automorphically covariant isometric pairs by identifying a complete set of joint unitary invariants. Notably, our results are novel even in the special case of rotation automorphisms ($V_1 V_2 = q V_2 V_1$ with $|q| = 1$).

papers.title: Symmetric Polynomials Method for the Multiple Loewner Chains
papers.abstract: We introduce the technique of Symmetric Polynomials in the study of Loewner chains driven by a family of stochastic particle systems including but not limited to Dyson Brownian motion. As a first application of this technique we obtain the phase transitions at the critical parameter $\kappa=4$ in terms of the behavior of a class of symmetric polynomials evolving in time. We obtain new proofs of the phase transitions, we also obtain new closed-form expressions relevant for the models. In addition, we apply this method for some initial deterministic multiple Loewner evolutions. Finally, as this is, to our knowledge, the first paper analyzing this method in the context of multiple Loewner chains driven by root-system based multivariate processes, we also give an overview of potential future applications of this technique in the study of these models.

papers.title: A new $\nu$-metric computational example for the diffusion equation with boundary control and point observation
papers.abstract: The $\nu$-metric used in robust control is computed for control systems with parametric uncertainty, governed by a diffusion equation in a bounded one-dimensional spatial region with boundary control and point observation.

papers.title: Genus $2$ pencils on surfaces with $p_g=K^2=1$, envelopes, and conics tangent to plane cubic curves
papers.abstract: We consider $(1,1)$-surfaces, namely, minimal compact complex surfaces $S$ with $p_g (S) =K_S^2=1$: for these the bicanonical map is a covering of degree $4$ of the plane $P^2$. And we answer a question posed by Meng Chen, whether they can contain a genus 2 pencil (this is the standard reason of failure of birationality of the bicanonical map). Our main theorem says that those which admit a genus 2 pencil form an irreducible subvariety of codimension $3$ in their moduli space $\frak M_{[1,1]}$; moreover, the general such surface admits exactly $24$ such pencils, corresponding to $12$ pencils of conics in $P^2$. The real fun is to relate this variety to the geometry of pencils of conics in the plane everywhere tangent to a cubic curve and a line. We investigate the corresponding variety $\cal{T}$ of triples and provide explicit equations using the classical theory of envelopes: among others, equations given in terms of the Weierstrass normal form of the cubic.

papers.title: Subclass of bi-univalent function associated to Chebyshev polynomial
papers.abstract: The Chebyshev polynomials are utilized in this study to define the subclass of the bi-univalent function. Also, Chebyshev polynomial bounds and Fekete-Szego inequalities for functions defined in the classes are established.

papers.title: Characterization of Asymptotically Smooth Chord-arc Curves
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit example of an asymptotically conformal chord-arc curve that fails to be asymptotically smooth. This implies that a function belonging to both the little Bloch space and $\mathrm{BMOA}$ does not necessarily lie in $\mathrm{VMOA}$, and that a strongly quasisymmetric homeomorphism which is symmetric is not necessarily strongly symmetric. We also provide a complete characterization of asymptotically smooth curves in terms of asymptotic conformality and uniform approximability.

papers.title: Semialgebraic interior layers in root closures of bounded-height integer polynomials
papers.abstract: Finite-degree root plots of bounded-height monic integer polynomials can exhibit gaps around interior points of their root closures. Outside the closed unit disk, these closures coincide with Mandelbrot sets for affine iterated function systems with collinear digits. We construct explicit semialgebraic interior layers, certified when finite inverse orbits enter canonical self-covering parallelograms. Such parallelograms exist exactly in the non-real lens, which contains the non-real locus precisely from twenty maps onward. Within the non-real lens, limits of each capture level are captured within two additional steps, optimally, and the layers recover the locus by closure. The layers expose persistent interior deficits: explicit quadratic parameters evade every finite level; sufficiently close distinct parameters have logarithmically growing capture depths; the underlying lattice obstruction yields degree-dependent root-free radii, explaining such gaps. For non-real parameters of modulus at least the square root of the number of maps, exact enclosure trees have sharp, alphabet-independent branching bounds.

papers.title: Invariant metrics of model domains near pseudoconcave points
papers.abstract: We give precise estimates of some holomorphically invariant infinitesimal metrics near a pseudoconcave points in a wide family of ``model'' domains for that situation in $\mathbb C^2$. This extends to metrics (rather distances) the authors' previous results from arXiv:2503.19754 and also takes into account defining functions more general than just power functions.
